The Data Room is where your uploaded files live, and where you decide what Caspr is allowed to use. Every file you bring in sits in one of three groups.

**Included** files are attached to your analyses by default — Caspr draws on them automatically alongside its own 25M+ curated sources, no extra step required each time you run an analysis.

**Excluded** files stay in your Data Room but sit out of every analysis unless you opt them in for a specific run. Nothing is deleted; it's simply not in default use, which keeps a one-off document from quietly bleeding into unrelated reports.

**Connected** sources — your own subscriptions to Bloomberg, Refinitiv, S&P Capital IQ, or PitchBook, feeding straight into your analyses — are coming soon. Not yet live, so don't expect them in the Data Room today.

Uploading your own data unlocks at the Business milestone. Once unlocked, it's how you fold proprietary numbers, internal decks, or a client's own data room into a Caspr analysis, rather than working from public sources alone — useful for due diligence, a client-specific business case, or any report that needs to reflect information Caspr can't find on its own.

Everything in the Data Room defaults to Private, stays under your control, and can be moved between Included and Excluded, or deleted outright, at any time.

This is the mechanic behind due diligence: upload the data room, mark the files Included, and Caspr wraps the market intelligence around them — the investment memo builds itself from your numbers plus Caspr's own sources, rather than from your numbers alone.

Caspr accepts four file types: PDF, XLSX, CSV, and DOCX. Upload several at once — there's no one-at-a-time limit, so a full data room's worth of files can go in together.

No file in hand? Paste a link instead — an article, a dataset, a public report — and Caspr fetches and indexes it the same way it would a document you'd uploaded directly, no separate step required.

Whatever you add, whether uploaded or linked, is folded into your analyses alongside Caspr's 25M+ curated sources, so your own numbers sit next to the market data Caspr already draws on, rather than existing as a separate, disconnected layer.

Data upload is a feature of the Business milestone — see what unlocks at Business if your account isn't there yet. Below that, you're working from Caspr's own sources alone.

A pasted link works best for something public and citable — a press release, a regulatory filing, a published dataset. For anything internal or confidential, upload the file directly rather than linking to it, so it stays private to your account from the start rather than depending on a link staying live.

Open the Data Room and use the add-file panel. On desktop, drop your files onto the upload box or click it to browse; on mobile, tap Upload files. No file in hand — paste a link underneath instead, and Caspr fetches and indexes it directly, without needing a downloaded copy first.

New files land at the top of your Included list immediately, each with its own progress bar while it processes. You don't have to wait for one to finish before adding the next — keep dropping files in and they'll queue and complete independently, so a large batch doesn't force you to sit and watch.

Every upload defaults to Private, kept to your account and visible only to you. If a file should be shared more broadly, change that from the file's menu once it lands — Private is the safe default, so there's nothing extra to set on the way in, only a deliberate choice to make afterward if you want otherwise.

Once a file has finished processing, it's ready to use — Caspr will draw on it automatically the next time you run an analysis, since new uploads land in Included by default. Move it to Excluded from the same menu if you'd rather keep it on hand without it feeding every future report.

Every file in your Data Room carries a Private or Public tag, visible at a glance on the row. Private is the default for every upload — the file stays to your account, and only you can see or use it in an analysis.

Making a file Public is always a deliberate choice. Select the file's checkbox and use Private/Public in the action toolbar — select several files at once and the toggle applies in bulk, so switching a whole batch takes one action instead of one file at a time. It never happens by default, and it's never a side effect of uploading or of running an analysis. Reversing it is just as easy: switching back to Private is always allowed instantly, with no confirmation step, because leaving something Public by mistake is the costly error, and Caspr is built to make that one easy to undo, not the one that's easy to make.

[VERIFY exact Public-file semantics — what "Public" makes visible, to whom, and under what conditions — with the team before publishing.]

Check or change a file's visibility any time from the Data Room's selection toolbar; there's no separate settings screen to hunt through.

Keep board-sensitive material — an internal deck, a client's data room, anything you wouldn't forward without thinking — set to Private by default and leave it there unless you have a specific reason to change it.

Included and Excluded are the two states a file can sit in while it stays in your Data Room — the difference is whether Caspr uses it automatically, not whether it's kept.

**Included** files are attached to your analyses by default. Upload something and it starts here, folded into every run alongside Caspr's own sources, unless you deliberately move it out.

**Excluded** files are kept, not deleted, but sit out of analyses unless you opt them into a specific run. Use this for a file you want on hand without it bleeding into every report — a one-off document, something outdated, or data relevant to only a single project.

Move a file between the two with its row checkbox: select one file, or several at once, and Include / Exclude buttons appear in the action toolbar above the list. Moving to Excluded is instant, since you're only narrowing what gets used and nothing downstream depends on it. Moving back to Included takes a one-tap confirm, since it reopens the file to default use across every future analysis — a small, deliberate step for a change with much wider reach. Drag-and-drop between the two groups still works too, for a single file at a time.

A typical case: last quarter's internal deck was useful when it was current, but you don't want it quietly informing every new analysis six months on. Select it and move it to Excluded instead of deleting it — it stays available to opt into a specific run later, without shaping reports it no longer belongs in.

Select the file's checkbox in your Data Room and choose Exclude from the action toolbar. It's instant, no confirmation needed, and the file stays exactly where it is, just out of the default set Caspr draws on. Excluded files are never attached to an analysis automatically; they only get pulled in if you opt them into that specific run.

The Data Room has no separate Archive — Exclude is its non-destructive declutter. This is the move to reach for whenever you're not sure you'll need the file long-term, rather than deleting it: nothing is lost, and nothing about the file changes except that Caspr stops assuming it's relevant. If you want it back in default rotation later, select it and choose Include from the same toolbar — that direction takes a one-tap confirm, since it re-opens the file to every analysis again.

Deleting is the one step you can't undo. Excluding is the one you can flip either direction, as often as you like — for a single file or several selected at once.

Select the file's checkbox in your Data Room and choose the red Delete in the action toolbar. A confirmation appears before anything happens, naming exactly what's about to go — "Delete 1 source?" for a single file, or the live count for whatever you've selected. Deletion is the one action here you can't reverse, so Caspr makes you pass through it deliberately.

The same toolbar handles more than one file at a time: select several rows, or use select-all, and Delete removes the whole selection in one confirm — the count in the prompt updates to match, so you always see exactly how many sources you're about to lose before you commit.

For a single file, that confirmation still offers you an out: Move to Excluded instead. Excluding takes the file out of default use without destroying it — it stays in your Data Room, available to opt into a specific analysis later. If you're deleting because you don't want the file used automatically, that's usually the answer you actually want, and it costs you nothing to keep.

Choose Delete permanently only when you mean the copy (or copies) gone for good. Once confirmed, Caspr cannot re-attach the file to any future analysis — not the current one, not one you run next year. There's no recovery and no second confirmation after the first.

Deleting has no effect on analyses that already used the file — the report you generated keeps its citations. Only future runs lose access to the source.

When in doubt, exclude first. Delete when you're certain.

Not yet — Connected sources are coming soon. Caspr will let you link your own subscriptions to Bloomberg, Refinitiv, S&P Capital IQ, and PitchBook, so that data feeds directly into your analyses alongside Caspr's curated sources. Until this ships, the Connected group in your Data Room is a placeholder. This page will update when it goes live.

Every file you upload defaults to Private and stays inside your Data Room, visible and usable only within your account unless you explicitly mark it Public. You control what happens to it from there: keep it Included so Caspr draws on it by default, move it to Excluded to keep it on hand without using it, or delete it outright, which removes it for good.

Making a file Public is always a deliberate choice; reversing that back to Private is instant and needs no confirmation, because the costly mistake is leaving something exposed, not protecting it too much.

For how your account itself is secured — password, two-factor, device sessions — see Security in your account settings.

Files you upload inside a Project default to Excluded, so a project's material stays out of your general analyses unless you opt it in.
